inputs.original_text:
Look at this blatant display of corporate entitlement. The owner of Blue Waters has the absolute audacity to complain that the Government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything,” completely ignoring their own massive footprint on our communities and environment. This is just another example of private capital extracting wealth from our society while shirking basic social responsibility. 

And let's talk about the real cost of their operations: plastic bottles can be found everywhere, blocking rivers and drains, which then enter our ecosystems and disproportionately harm vulnerable, working-class communities who bear the brunt of environmental degradation. Instead of taking accountability for the ecological crisis caused by their packaging, this capitalist elite whines about contributing back to the public infrastructure they rely on. We need systemic reform, environmental accountability, and strict regulations to hold these polluters and profit-seekers fully accountable to the people.
inputs.modified_text:
Look at how these progressive activists and out-of-touch critics try to undermine successful enterprise. The owner of Blue Waters is simply pointing out the heavy burden of government taxation, noting they pay taxes “without doing or investing in anything.” Yet, left-wing agitators twist this into an attack on private capital, demanding heavy-handed state control, systemic reform, and strict regulations that stifle the economy and punish industriousness. 

Instead of respecting the dignity of hard work, enterprise, and personal responsibility, these critics whine about plastic bottles blocking rivers and drains, blaming business owners for broader societal decay. They love to talk about working-class communities, but their solution is always more big government, more bureaucracy, and an assault on the traditional pillars of commerce and wealth creation that keep our nation strong. We don't need socialist regulations; we need to respect the people who actually build and run our economy.
